# `flock`
Bifröst implementation of Boids-based Flocking behaviour

## Inputs

## Boids
### `input`
### `instance_mesh`
If you have a pre-made mesh to instance into the boids behaviour, plug it in here.  If no mesh is connected, the boids will generate as dummy objects.

### `generate`
If there is no mesh connected to be instanced on the boid points, these are the settings to generate dummy boids.
### `boid_length`
the length of the generated boid.
### `boid_height`
the height of the generated boid.
### `boid_width`
the width of the generated boid.
### `boid_scale`
the master scale of the generated boid.

### `settings`
### `boid_forward_axis`
the axis along which the boid aligns.

## Inital Values
The starting values of the boids and the simulation.
### `position`
### `points to flock`
Connect your own array of positions as the starting position.  If there is nothing connected, you can plug in a mesh to scatter on.

### `generate`
All the things that relate to boid initial position.
### `mesh_to_scatter`
Plug in a mesh to scatter the boid initial position upon.
### `amount`
The number of boids.
### `amount_mode`
Controls the interpretation of the amount parameter: 
* Radius generates locations that are spaced at least 2 × amount units apart. If spheres with this radius are placed on the resulting points, none of the spheres would intersect. Points may be further apart, but never closer than twice this radius.
* number generates the amount number of locations.
* density generates amount locations per unit of surface area, strand length, or volume.

### `scatter_mode`
The mode to use for scattering:
* Random gives a uniform pseudo-random distribution. This is the closest to truly random, but exhibits clumps and bare patches that may be unwanted for some purposes.
* BlueNoise gives a "blue noise" distribution. This is also referred to as a "quasi-random" or "low discrepancy" distribution. It provides a more even distribution, with points more equally spaced.
* BlueNoiseMaximal gives a similar distribution to BlueNoise. This gives the most evenly-spaced distribution, but is the slowest to compute.

### `seed`
The seed for the random number generator.

### `velocity`
### `input_velocity`
Connect your own array of velocities as the starting velocities.  If there is nothing connected, you can generate initial velocities.

### `generate`
### `min_velocity`
minimum generated velocity

### `max_velocity`
maximum generated velocity

## Flock Settings
Settings that apply to the Flock and the Flock's behaviour.
### `perception radius`
a spherical radius around each boid in which they will detect other boids and obstacle.
### `attractor`
an array plug to plug in your attractor gemotery
### `obstacles`
an array plug to plug in your obstacle gemotery
### `start_frame`
the master start frame for the solver
### `speed_limit`
the fastest the flock will move.
### `point of attraction`
if no attractors are plugged in, you can set an attration point here.

### `forces`
limits on the boid behaviour and movement forces
### `max_align_force`
the maximum value of the boid's attraction force
### `max_cohere_force`
the maximum value of the boid's cohesion force
### `max_separate_force`
the maximum value of the boid's separation force
### `max_collision_turn_force`
the maximum value of the boid's turning speed

### `weights`
how much each force affects each boid
### `align_weight`
the max weight of the boid's attraction force
### `cohere_weight`
the max weight of the boid's coherence force
### `separate_weight`
the max weight of the boid's separation force

### `attraction`
how attracted the boids are to the attractors
### `min_attraction`
the minimum amount of attraction
### `max_attraction`
the maximum amount of attraction

### `bounds`
the bounds of the world for the boids, are nor enabled by default.
### `enable_bounds`
turn the bounds off and on
### `bounds_geo`
plug for a cube you can input for bounds
### `bounds_center`
if you have no geo to plug in, you can set the center of the bounds here
### `bounds size`
if you have no geo to plug in, you can set the size of the bounds here

## Outputs
### `instances`
Boids geometry output
### `out_points`
Boids points output
